text: Appius governed four sturdy sons, five daughters, that great establishment, and all those clients, though he was both old and blind. For he kept his mind at full stretch like a bow, and never gave in to old age by growing slack.
author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
speaker: Cato
reference: Treatises on Friendship and Old Age
location: Rome or his villa at Tusculum, Italy (presumed)
